question: MI-13 Democratic Primary Winner
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins the nomination for the Democratic Party to contest the MI-13 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The Democratic primary will take place on August 4, 2026.

If no nominee is announced by November 3, 2026, 11:59PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Democrat sources, including https://democrats.org/.

Any replacement of the nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

"Other" means any option not listed here.
research:
# MI-13 Democratic primary: research summary as of 2026-07-17

The ballot is effectively a two-way race between incumbent Shri Thanedar and state Rep. Donavan McKinney. The only public poll shows a statistical tie, and the most recent market price I could date with confidence is from early May.

## 1. Resolution source
- The criteria name democrats.org and "a consensus of official Democrat sources." Party sites don't usually list primary results. In practice the winner will come from AP calls and then official certification by Wayne County and the Michigan Board of State Canvassers.
- 2026-07-17: Nothing has been decided. The primary is on 2026-08-04, so no nominee has been announced. I did not fetch democrats.org, because it posts no data for this race.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet.
- 2026-05-19: Ballotpedia listed six Democrats running: Thanedar, McKinney, Shelby Campbell, Anthony Carbonaro, John Goci and Naz Hassan. [Ballotpedia](https://news.ballotpedia.org/2026/05/19/rep-thanedar-faces-sanders-backed-challenger-in-michigans-13th-district-democratic-primary/)
- Mid-2026: BridgeDetroit reports that only Thanedar and McKinney are on the Democratic primary ballot. Mary Waters (Detroit City Council member, who finished second in the 2024 primary) and John Goci were kept off the ballot and are running as write-ins. That article does not mention Campbell, Carbonaro or Hassan, which suggests they are not on the printed ballot, but I could not confirm this directly. [BridgeDetroit](https://www.bridgedetroit.com/?p=233698)
- "Person A" is not a real candidate, as far as I can find.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- July 9-15, 2026: Data for Progress poll of 324 likely voters, margin of error about ±5. Thanedar 46%, McKinney 42%, undecided 12-13%. After respondents read candidate bios, McKinney led 48-41. The release date looks to be around July 16-17. [Drop Site on X](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2078287830179045864), [PredictionEdge](https://www.predictionedge.com/elections/us-house/michigan-district-13-democratic-primary/)
- July 2026: Rep. Summer Lee and the Democratic Socialists of America endorsed McKinney. [Metro Times](https://metrotimes.com/news/another-progressive-member-of-congress-backs-donavan-mckinney-over-shri-thanedar)
- Thanedar has endorsements from Hakeem Jeffries and Reps. Cleo Fields, Greg Stanton, Joe Neguse and Raja Krishnamoorthi. [Ballotpedia](https://news.ballotpedia.org/2026/05/19/rep-thanedar-faces-sanders-backed-challenger-in-michigans-13th-district-democratic-primary/)
- Mid-2026, money:
  - Thanedar had about $5M cash on hand, largely self-funded.
  - McKinney had raised about $1M and refuses corporate PAC money.
  - Critics point to Thanedar spending $930K of official office funds on advertising, his corporate PAC money and support linked to AIPAC. [BridgeDetroit](https://www.bridgedetroit.com/?p=233698)
- Protect Progress, a crypto super PAC affiliated with Fairshake, ran ads backing Thanedar. Crypto-trade outlets put the spending at $1M, later over $2M. I found no FEC confirmation dated before July 17. [Currency Analytics](https://thecurrencyanalytics.com/altcoins/crypto-pac-drops-1m-on-michigan-democratic-primary-shaking-up-thanedar-mckinney-race-277855)
- 2025: Bernie Sanders, Rashida Tlaib and SEIU Michigan endorsed McKinney. [Michigan Advance](https://michiganadvance.com/briefs/donavan-mckinney-gets-endorsement-of-bernie-sanders-in-effort-to-primary-shri-thanedar/)

## 4. Base rates
- House incumbents rarely lose primaries, usually fewer than 2-3% per cycle. That rate is higher in open-ideology challenges backed by well-funded progressive or DSA groups, such as Bush and Bowman losing in 2024 and Cori Bush winning as a challenger in 2020.
- MI-13 history:
  - 2022: Thanedar won a crowded open primary with a plurality of about 28%.
  - 2024: He beat Waters 54.9% to 33.8%, after Adam Hollier was disqualified over his petitions. [Ballotpedia](https://news.ballotpedia.org/2026/05/19/rep-thanedar-faces-sanders-backed-challenger-in-michigans-13th-district-democratic-primary/)
- The general election is rated Safe Democratic, so the primary effectively decides the seat.
- Write-in candidates almost never win Michigan congressional primaries.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-05-03: Lines.com reported Polymarket at about 69% for Thanedar. [Lines.com](https://www.lines.com/prediction-markets/elections/mi-13-democratic-primary-winner)
- Kalshi runs a market on this race (KXMI13D), but the page returned an error and I could not retrieve a price dated on or before July 17. [Kalshi](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxmi13d/mi13-democratic-nominee/kxmi13d-26)
- PredictionEdge combines the market odds. I could not confirm a dated snapshot from before July 17, so I am not reporting its numbers. [PredictionEdge](https://www.predictionedge.com/elections/us-house/michigan-district-13-democratic-primary/)
- I found no Manifold market or expert handicapper rating for the primary.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Late July: more outside spending (the crypto PAC, possibly AIPAC-linked groups or progressive PACs) and more endorsements are likely.
- Possible new public polls. Data for Progress is the only one so far.
- WDIV's Flashpoint and other debates or interviews in late July and early August.
- Absentee and early voting is already under way in Michigan.
- 2026-08-04: primary day. The AP call is expected that night or the next day.
- After that: Wayne County canvass, then state certification. A close margin could trigger a recount and delay the result.

forecasts.reasoning:
error of about ±5. After respondents read candidate bios, McKinney led 48-41. DFP leans progressive, so the true race may favor Thanedar slightly more, but this is close to a toss-up.
- **Market, May 3, 2026:** Polymarket had Thanedar at about 69%. That price is before the poll.
- **Ballot, mid-2026:** Only Thanedar and McKinney are on the ballot, so the anti-incumbent vote is consolidated. Mary Waters is running as a write-in, which could siphon a little of that vote, which helps Thanedar.
- **Endorsements:** McKinney has Sanders, Tlaib, SEIU, Summer Lee and DSA. Thanedar has Jeffries and other House members.
- **Money:** Thanedar holds the overwhelming spending advantage, and crypto PAC spending reportedly exceeds $1-2M on his behalf.

**(e) Unexpected scenario:** The incumbent losing is a realistic outcome, not a fringe one. The truly unexpected case would be a successful Waters write-in campaign, or a disqualification or legal issue, sending the result to "Other." That chance is about 1-2%.

**Reasoning:** I start from the May market price of 69% for Thanedar. The only poll shows a near-tie in a head-to-head race, and bio-informed responses favor McKinney, so I move down. The money gap, the pollster's lean and the write-in split partly offset that. I land at about 58% for Thanedar and 39% for McKinney, with small amounts on the remaining options.

**How I moved:** I started from roughly 70/30 for Thanedar, based on the May market price and the incumbency rate for challenged incumbents. The near-tied poll, with McKinney leading after bios, moved me about 12 points toward McKinney.
